strongest_result: Deterministic O_k(m+n+n^(k+0.3)) prescribed vertex-disjoint shortest-path detection for every fixed k>=3 on every positive-weight DAG in the immutable source addition/comparison model, with all new algebraic operands O_k(log(n+2)) bits and their elementary arithmetic charged. The k=3, delta=0.7 consequence fully and positively resolves AVW Open Problem 3. The original-weight bit-cost and arbitrary parallel-arc input-scan qualifications are explicit and unchanged.

importance.reason: The theorem gives a polynomial dense exponent saving for the full unrestricted original and for every fixed k>=3. AVW explicitly identifies the same baseline as persisting from the 1980 tuple-graph approach and asks this exact improvement. Prescribed routing and individually shortest paths are central algorithmic graph problems, so the result has value beyond an arbitrary special-case exercise.

novelty.reason: Against the precise inspected tuple-graph, shortest-path and closure theorems, the first-context-in-R output partition and charged rectangular schedule supply a new algorithmic bound. The fresh current primary search found no equivalent full theorem. Established recursion and multiplication tools are explicitly excluded from the novelty claim; the bounded search is not asserted to prove global priority.

technical_depth.reason: The dependency-safe output partition and complete packing charge are substantive and sufficient for mathematical innovation. Their core is nevertheless a compact adaptation of chronological divide and conquer to a known tuple recurrence. The stronger numerical exponent then follows from existing rectangular multiplication and standard rational interpolation. The packet does not yet demonstrate a broader new algebraic or structural mechanism, and I cannot confidently assess this level of new technique alone as strong for STOC.

breadth_or_consequence.reason: The theorem covers all fixed k and arbitrary label-specific common-order edge graphs, including ordinary prescribed disjoint paths and weighted shortest paths. That is a meaningful consequence. The proved improvement is dense-instance detection on DAGs, with O_k(n^k) state storage; there is no established extension to cyclic digraphs, matching lower bound, optimal exponent, or further independent TCS application in this packet. Whether the demonstrated consequences alone support a broad STOC case remains uncertain.

This referee reconstructed those steps and independently passed 4,718 full-state and 360 original weighted-path comparisons. The packet is sufficient for mathematical verification; manuscript layout and citation/build checks remain future gates.
